meta.description: Per-station emissions dossier: CO2 intensity and absolute CO2 (CEA CO2 Baseline DB v22), unit-wise FGD status and SO2 deadlines (CEA Nov 2023 sheet + MoEFCC 2025 rules), fly-ash generation/utilisation (CEA 2021-22 station-wise, TN also Apr-Sep 2022), MoEFCC 2015 stack norms per unit vintage, nearby CAAQMS (TN), pollution incidents (TN), measured SO2 2021 (TN, RTI via CREA), and labelled estimates of annual CO2/SO2/NOx/PM (TN).

coverage.tamil_nadu: all coal/lignite/gas/naphtha/nuclear stations incl. retired / under construction
coverage.rest_of_india: coal, lignite, gas, diesel, oil stations in the CEA CO2 DB with capacity or generation > 0; FGD/fly-ash/coal-receipt joins are fuzzy and flagged

join_notes: FGD units are matched to CO2-DB units by state + unit MW + commissioning date within 75 days + name similarity; TN uses a manual station map.
Fly ash, coal-receipt and OSM coordinate joins outside TN are fuzzy name matches; each carries a 'match' or 'loc_precision' note. Nulls mean no confident match, not 'no data'.
NCTPS Stage II and Stage III share one CEA CO2-DB row ('NORTH CHENNAI EXTENSION'); they are split here by unit.

so2_cross_check.note: CREA (Oct 2021) satellite-based 2019 SO2 hotspot emissions: Neyveli 299 kt, Chennai 142 kt, Tuticorin 52 kt, Mettur 47 kt. The FY2025-26 mass-balance estimates here sum to roughly Neyveli 240 kt, Chennai (NCTPS I-III + Vallur) 125 kt, Mettur 55 kt and Tuticorin 115 kt (Tuticorin now includes SEPC, commissioned 2021, plus higher Mutiara/NTPL output). The RTI stack concentrations (Apr-Jun 2021) imply 3-10x lower totals, so the mass balance is the headline (so2_t_best) and the concentration-based figure is kept as a lower bound.

norms_summary.compliance: within 2 years of notification (by 2017-12-07), later category-wise deadlines for SO2 (see fgd_units.json)

norms_summary.nox_note: 300 mg/Nm3 in 2015 notification; relaxed to 450 by G.S.R. 662(E) dated 19-10-2020

norms_summary.vintage: installed from 2017-01-01 (incl. units with EC and under construction at notification)

gas_turbine_nox_norms.stack_height: H = 14 * Q^0.3 (Q SO2 kg/hr), min 30 m

meta.licence: Derived from Government of India publications (CEA, MoEFCC, CPCB, TNPCB) with attribution; CREA report (CC BY); OSM (ODbL).

nctps-1.fgd_context: Nov-2023 CEA sheet is the latest unit-wise status. MoEFCC 11-Jul-2025 amendment: Category A units must meet SO2 limits by 31-12-2027; Category B are decided case by case (31-12-2028 if applicable); Category C units are exempt from SO2 limits if they meet the stack-height rule by 31-12-2029. TNPGCL reportedly put FGD tendering on hold after July 2025 (DTNext, 2025-07-14).
nctps-1.est_method: CO2: CEA CO2 Baseline v22 FY2025-26 (station-specific, CEA-computed). Heat input = CO2 / (fuel EF x oxidation), converted to HHV; dry flue gas = heat input x US EPA Method 19 F-factor corrected to 6% O2. SO2 (a) mass balance: fuel t x S% x 2 x 0.95 x (1 - removal); (b) where 2021 RTI stack data exist: flue gas x mean measured mg/Nm3. NOx: flue gas x assumed 450 mg/Nm3 (250 CFBC) = mid-range of 300-600 mg/Nm3 achievable with combustion modification. PM: fuel t x ash% x 0.8 fly-ash fraction x (1 - ESP efficiency 99.7% pre-2004 / 99.9% newer). Fuel t: CEA monthly coal statements (coal) or CEA fly-ash report 2021-22 scaled by generation (lignite). Run-rate: FY2026-27 YTD gross generation from CEA/NPP DGR, annualised and converted to net with an assumed auxiliary consumption, times FY2025-26 intensities.
est_caveats: Estimates, not measurements. Sulphur contents are generic: domestic 0.45% (NEERI/NITI 2025: Indian coal <0.5% S), imported 0.6% (assumed), Neyveli lignite 0.8% (published analyses: <1% S).
NOx and PM concentrations are assumptions; the actual OCEMS data are not public.
Apr-Sep YTD annualisation ignores seasonality (monsoon and wind season depress coal PLF).
